name: Madame Torré
description:
We had slept beneath rows of cypresses that formed avenues running across the misty heath. Our bedrolls soaked with dew and sleep still heavy upon our eyes, we were startled into wakefulness when out of the fast-clearing air we espied a tower that had not stood there at the sun's setting.

It seemed ancient but fair, with well-hewn stones forming its sides, leading up to a lofty chamber high above the grass. Lengths of bright cloth hung from the sills of the windows and played merrily in the breeze, their motion seeming to form gestures of beckoning. We felt drawn upward, but also felt a growing dread as we mounted the stairs.

Even after all these years, I still find it hard to speak of what passed there. I saw faces from across the ocean. I heard voices from the top of the mountain. I felt fears and sorrows of loved ones left behind. Each of us saw and heard and felt these things in turn, and though we were brought low by them, she - for these were of course, the doings of Madame Torré - ever met our gaze with a painted smile. Her outward kindness hid something - a darkness? a power? a hunger?

And so we descended, pressed at our backs by her well-wishing. And in a last, parting kindness that somehow cut into me, I turned to hear her voice calling from her high window, "hey love, you forgot your glove." And she flung it down.

⁂ ⁂ ⁂

Madame Torré is first and foremost mysterious. Her origins and motivations are not known. What is known is that her tower appears where it is least looked for, vanishes just as abruptly, and that those who visit her in her high chamber emerge changed.

With her crystal, she possesses great powers of far-seeing (whether spatial, temporal or both is up to you). She will happily engage these powers for the benefit of her visitors, but it is her strong tendency to focus on inconvenient truths and unwelcome news.

Whether she is rendering a service or extracting some strange power from the revelation of these distressing visions, none can tell. From whence she has gained this power is also unknown, and whether she might ever choose to wield it toward other ends is a fearful prospect.
